title: A dictated notification reply must land in an editable draft
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `A11`.

## The problem
In-app dictation already lands in an editable field the user confirms (DictateLink into TypeSheet and the reply sheet). The notification Reply action does not: Shared/AgentNotifications.swift registers a UNTextInputNotificationAction whose button is "Send", so watchOS dictation fires the recognised text straight at a live agent prompt. That is the one path that breaks "review before dispatch", and it is the path used when it matters most — from a raised wrist, mid-run.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Choosing Reply on a watch agent notification opens the app's own review sheet with the dictated text pre-filled and editable; nothing reaches the session until Send is tapped
- [ ] Approve, Decline and Stop are unchanged — each is one unambiguous key and stays one tap from the notification
- [ ] Cancelling the review sends nothing, leaves the agent blocked, and leaves the notification still actionable
- [ ] The issue is explicitly hand-checked on a real Apple Watch and says so: an agent cannot verify that the mic opens or that the banner behaves

## Where it stands today — `missing`
Shared/AgentNotifications.swift:107-113 — `let reply = UNTextInputNotificationAction(identifier: Action.reply.rawValue, title: Action.reply.title, options: [], textInputButtonTitle: "Send", textInputPlaceholder: "Reply to the agent")`, with `options: []` (no `.foreground`), so the system text field still dispatches straight through. Shared/AgentNotifications.swift:66-68 confirms the handler sends whatever was typed: `case .reply: let text = (typed ?? "")… return text.isEmpty ? nil : (text, nil)`. Approve/Decline/Stop remain plain one-tap actions (Shared/AgentNotifications.swift:117-125), which is the unchanged half the acceptance asks for.

**What is actually left:** Turn Reply into a foreground action that opens the app's own review sheet pre-filled and editable, keep cancel = send nothing / notification still actionable, and record the hand-check on a real Apple Watch.

title: Clear agent events, one by one and all at once
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `A12`.

## The problem
"In our notifications or the events, we don't have an option to clear them or remove them one by one." Both lists are read-only: EventsView on the watch and the Events section of MonitorTab on the phone render store.events with no swipe, no delete and no Clear all. The daemon only offers GET and POST /events, so ~/.mesh/agent-events.jsonl just grows and the newest 100 are shown forever.

## Acceptance
- [ ] meshd gains DELETE /events/:id and DELETE /events behind the same auth as every other route, rewriting ~/.mesh/agent-events.jsonl, and advertises a new capability string so an older daemon never gets a dead button
- [ ] Watch EventsView supports swipe-to-delete on a row plus a "Clear all" with confirmation; the iOS MonitorTab Events section does the same
- [ ] A cleared event stays cleared across an app relaunch AND a daemon restart, and does not reappear through the phone relay's snapshot
- [ ] On a daemon without the capability the clear affordances are absent rather than failing, and a scripts/check-*.sh proves the route exists in server.ts and that both clients call it

## Where it stands today — `missing`
install/payload/meshd/server.ts:987-988 — only `GET /events` and `POST /events` are routed; the only DELETE handlers in the file are killPane/kill at install/payload/meshd/server.ts:1035 and 1040. No new capability string is advertised. Watch/WatchViews.swift:486-511 — EventsView is a bare `List(store.events.reversed())` with no ForEach, no `.onDelete`, no swipeActions and no Clear all. iOS/ContentView.swift:77-99 — the MonitorTab Events section is a read-only `ForEach(store.events.reversed())`; the only `.onDelete` calls in that file are for machines (iOS/ContentView.swift:1160) and quick commands (iOS/ContentView.swift:1178).

**What is actually left:** All of it: DELETE /events/:id and DELETE /events with the jsonl rewrite, a capability string, both clients' delete UI, relay-snapshot correctness, and the check script.

title: Decide the future of Screen peek: keep, merge into Control, or remove

- [ ] If Screen peek goes, ScreenPeekView and any relay path left with no caller go with it, and sh scripts/check-all.sh still passes

title: First-class /commands, bash-mode ! and file-reference @ in the terminal
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `A9`.

## The problem
Driving Claude Code or Codex from a phone or a wrist means typing "/", "!" and "@" — the three characters the on-screen keyboards make hardest to reach and the ones with the highest payoff. Neither app knows they exist: quick commands are plain shell strings and there is no slash-command list anywhere.

## Acceptance
- [ ] When a session's agentType is claude or codex, the compose surface offers a "/" chip that lists that agent's slash commands and inserts the chosen one into the draft — never straight down the wire
- [ ] "!" and "@" have their own one-tap inserts on both the iPhone compose surface and the watch terminal key bar
- [ ] Everything inserted lands in the editable draft, so it is completed and reviewed before sending (AGENTS.md design principle 4)
- [ ] On a plain shell session (agentType nil) the agent-specific chips are absent rather than present-and-inert
- [ ] Proof against a real Claude Code session in a mux pane: tapping "/", picking a command, then Send actually runs it

## Where it stands today — `missing`
grep for `slashCommand|slash command|bashMode` across iOS/TerminalView.swift and Watch/WatchViews.swift returns zero hits. `agentType` is read in those files only for usage-limit gating (iOS/TerminalView.swift:407, 465, 489; Watch/WatchViews.swift:920, 933) — never to branch the compose surface. The iOS quick commands are plain strings from `store.quickCommands` (iOS/TerminalView.swift:674), and the watch key bar (Watch/WatchViews.swift:1246-1261) has no "/", "!" or "@" chip.

**What is actually left:** Everything: the per-agent slash-command list and inserter, the ! and @ one-tap inserts on both clients, draft-only insertion, and the nil-agentType absence rule.

**Depends on:** One compose surface per session instead of four ways to send text

title: Give Read mode visible pan buttons on both axes
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `A5`.

## The problem
Arya likes Read mode but asked for "small minimal buttons to move around ... left and right as well, so that we can move to any corner of the screen". Today there is no button for any direction: the crown pans up and down, and sideways panning is hidden in invisible left/right tap zones announced only by a hint that fades after three seconds. Once the hint is gone, half the picture is unreachable.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The inspector in Watch/RemoteView.swift shows persistent minimal controls for up, down, left and right, each at least WatchTouch.minWidth x minHeight, that do not cover the middle-third exit target
- [ ] From centre at 6x, repeated taps reach all four corners of the display; clampedPan stops exactly at each edge and the button disables (or plays .failure) once there
- [ ] Each tap calls fetchRegionNow() on a direct route so the picture moves on the next frame instead of up to 2s later
- [ ] The crown keeps its current vertical pan, and the invisible side zones are either kept deliberately or removed — not left as a second undocumented input

## Where it stands today — `missing`
Watch/RemoteView.swift:521-608 — the inspector's only visible overlay is `inspectZoomChips` (Watch/RemoteView.swift:571, 624-645: −/+/zoom label only). Horizontal panning is still invisible tap thirds at Watch/RemoteView.swift:573-581 (`if point.x < third { pan(-1…) } else if point.x > geo.size.width - third { pan(1…) } else { inspecting = false }`), and the only announcement is the 3-second hint at Watch/RemoteView.swift:557-565 + 601-606 (`Text("Crown ↕ · sides ↔ · tap middle to exit")`, then `withAnimation { showInspectHint = false }`). Vertical pan is crown-only (Watch/RemoteView.swift:584-596). No up/down/left/right buttons exist.

**What is actually left:** The four persistent WatchTouch-sized buttons, plus disabled/.failure state at each edge. The plumbing they would sit on already exists and works: `clampedPan` + `panStep` (Watch/RemoteView.swift:663-668), edge `.failure` haptic (Watch/RemoteView.swift:671-675), and `fetchRegionNow()` on the direct route (Watch/RemoteView.swift:674, 687-690).

title: Give the full-keyboard modifier row the same glyphs, and add fn
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `A1`.

## The problem
On the watch's "Every key" keyboard (Control > Mac > Keyboard > Every key) the modifier row still spells out "cmd / shift / opt / ctrl", which wraps mid-word inside a 40mm chip and reads as a layout bug — and fn is missing entirely. One level up, the Keys screen already shows the real keycap glyphs, so the same four modifiers look like two different features depending on which screen you reached them from.

## Acceptance
- [ ] RemoteKeyboardView.modifierRow in Watch/RemoteView.swift renders the same five chips as RemoteKeysView (⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃ fn), reading RemoteKeysView.modifiers rather than a second literal ["cmd","shift","opt","ctrl"] array
- [ ] Each chip carries accessibilityLabel = the spoken word (Command/Shift/Option/Control/Function) and accessibilityValue "held" or "off", matching RemoteKeysView
- [ ] scripts/check-mesh-input.sh asserts BOTH modifier rows against mesh-input's MODIFIERS table — today its awk only reads the one `static let modifiers:` table, so this row could carry an unmappable name forever
- [ ] xcodebuild -project MeshWatch.xcodeproj -scheme 'MeshWatch Watch App' -destination 'generic/platform=watchOS Simulator' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build succeeds

## Where it stands today — `missing`
Watch/RemoteView.swift:1425-1437 — `private var modifierRow` still does `ForEach(["cmd", "shift", "opt", "ctrl"], id: \.self) { mod in Button(mod) ... }`: spelled-out words, only four entries (no fn), no `.accessibilityLabel`/`.accessibilityValue`. The glyph table it should read lives at Watch/RemoteView.swift:1180-1186 (`static let modifiers` = ⌘/⇧/⌥/⌃/fn with spoken names) and is consumed only by RemoteKeysView at Watch/RemoteView.swift:1141-1155. scripts/check-mesh-input.sh:93 — `mods=$(awk '/static let modifiers:/,/^    \]/' "$VIEW" ...)` reads only that one table, so the second row is unasserted.

**What is actually left:** Rewrite RemoteKeyboardView.modifierRow to iterate RemoteKeysView.modifiers (glyph + spoken + held/off), and extend check-mesh-input.sh to also parse the KEYBOARD-view row against MODIFIERS in install/payload/bin/mesh-input.swift:116. The Keys-screen half the issue calls already-done is genuinely done.

title: Insert the Mac's clipboard into a session, not just the iPhone's
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `A10, buried-readPhoneClipboard`.

## The problem
The watch session screen has "Insert iPhone clipboard" but nothing for the Mac's own clipboard — so copy a path, a URL or a stack trace on the Mac and the wrist cannot paste it back into the agent that needs it. The daemon already serves GET /clipboard, and RemoteControl.pullClipboard() already reads it over both the direct and the relay route; only the button into a session is missing. (The backlog's "readPhoneClipboard has zero callers" note is now stale — AgentLiveView calls store.insertPhoneClipboard(); this is the other direction.)

## Acceptance
- [ ] AgentLiveView in Watch/WatchViews.swift gains an "Insert Mac clipboard" action beside the iPhone one, delivered through the same session send path
- [ ] It inserts with no trailing newline, like the iPhone path — the text sits on the prompt line so it can be read before it is sent
- [ ] It works when the watch is relaying through the phone, and on failure says which of "the Mac's clipboard is empty" or "no answer from <host>" happened — never a blank line
- [ ] A machine whose daemon cannot serve the clipboard hides the button rather than offering one that fails

## Where it stands today — `missing`
Watch/WatchViews.swift:1010-1016 — the Actions section has exactly one clipboard button, `Button { Task { await store.insertPhoneClipboard() } } label: { Label("Insert iPhone clipboard", …) }`; there is no Mac counterpart. `RemoteControl.pullClipboard()` (Watch/RemoteView.swift:381-390) is not buried but is wired only to a viewer, not a sender: its single caller is `Button("Read Mac clipboard")` in RemoteClipboardView at Watch/RemoteView.swift:1327-1331, which assigns to `@State macClipboard` and renders it as Text (Watch/RemoteView.swift:1336-1339). No path sends that text to a session. Note: CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased entry "Read the Mac's clipboard from the watch … and drop it into a session" overstates this — the drop-into-a-session half does not exist.

**What is actually left:** The "Insert Mac clipboard" action in AgentLiveView on the same send path, no trailing newline, relay support, distinct empty-vs-no-answer errors, and hiding it when the daemon lacks the capability.

title: Keep a Mac awake, controllable and capturable with the lid closed
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `A3`.

## The problem
Close the MacBook lid and the machine sleeps: sessions stall, the watch shows it offline, and any agent mid-run stops. Even if it stayed awake, a lid-closed Mac with no external display has no framebuffer to grab, so /screen.jpg — the trackpad preview and Read mode both — would go blank at exactly the moment the wrist is the only way in. Arya wants to shut the lid and keep working.

## Acceptance
- [ ] meshd can hold the Mac awake with the lid closed (a managed caffeinate/pmset lifetime it owns), off by default, toggled from Control > Mac > System, with the state reported on /health or /doctor so no client is guessing — and released by `mesh uninstall` so nothing keeps a Mac awake after the daemon is gone
- [ ] Proof pasted into the PR: with the hold on and the lid shut, GET /agents still answers and POST /agents/<s>/send still reaches a live mux session 5 minutes later
- [ ] A written finding records what a real lid-closed Mac returns from /screen.jpg and /displays, and the chosen fix (virtual display, or an explicit no-display state) either serves a real frame or returns a structured error
- [ ] Watch Read mode and iOS/RemoteScreenView.swift show that named reason ("this Mac has no display while the lid is shut") rather than a grey box or an endless spinner

## Where it stands today — `missing`
Repo-wide grep for `caffeinate|keepAwake|keep_awake|clamshell|lid closed|lid-closed` across install/, Watch/, iOS/, Shared/, scripts/, docs/ returns zero hits (only pmset uses are the sleep actions at install/payload/meshd/input.ts:188-189). Watch/RemoteView.swift:1294-1307 — RemoteSystemView offers only Lock/Sleep display/Screen saver/Sleep Mac, no awake toggle. install/payload/meshd/input.ts:254-261 — `/displays` returns a generic `could not read displays` error, not a named no-display state. Watch/RemoteView.swift:544-555 — the inspector falls back to `remote.screenError` or "Fetching screen…"/"No screen yet — still trying", never a lid-shut reason.

**What is actually left:** All four bullets: the managed caffeinate/pmset lifetime owned by meshd, its state on /health or /doctor, release on `mesh uninstall`, the lid-closed /screen.jpg + /displays finding, and the named reason in Watch Read mode and iOS/RemoteScreenView.swift.

title: Lock the Mac from the wrist and unlock it by typing the password
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `A2`.

## The problem
"Lock screen" already works from Control > Mac > System, but once the Mac is locked there is no way back in from the phone or the watch — you have to walk to the machine. Arya wants the round trip: close the screen remotely, and get a quick password dialog on the phone or watch that opens it again.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A written verdict lands in docs/ with pasted output from a real macOS 26 machine, recording whether synthetic keystrokes can reach the login window while Secure Input is active — this is measured, not assumed
- [ ] If they can: POST /system {action:"unlock"} accepts a password that never reaches a log line, a query string, a file on the Mac, or UserDefaults; the phone holds it via Shared/SecureStore.swift (Keychain); entering it while the Mac is locked returns it to the desktop within 10s
- [ ] If they cannot: the Lock button says so before you tap it ("you will need the Mac's own keyboard to get back in") and no dead Unlock button ships
- [ ] A scripts/check-*.sh fails if a password value can reach a log statement, a URL, or UserDefaults on either side

## Where it stands today — `missing`
install/payload/meshd/input.ts:187-194 — `SYSTEM_ACTIONS` contains only displaysleep, sleep, lock, screensaver, shutdown, restart; there is no `unlock`. Watch/RemoteView.swift:1300 — `Button("Lock screen") { remote.system("lock") }` with no warning text about needing the Mac's own keyboard. Repo-wide grep for `secure input|loginwindow|login window` across *.md/*.swift/*.ts/*.sh returns zero hits, so no docs/ verdict exists. No scripts/check-*.sh asserts password non-leakage (scripts/ listing has no such file).

**What is actually left:** Everything: the measured macOS 26 Secure-Input finding in docs/, then either the unlock route + Keychain-held password + leak-check script, or the honest warning on the Lock button.

title: Name the five controls on the watch Control screen
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `A4`.

## The problem
The row under the trackpad is five bare glyphs. Asked what the third one did, the person who uses this every day said he could not understand the hand symbol — and could not say which of the two hands he meant. The glyphs improved recently (gyroscope, padlock), but there is still no text on any of them and no legend anywhere, while one of those buttons holds the Mac's physical mouse button down until it is pressed again.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Each of the five controls (Click, Air mouse, Drag lock, Type, More) shows a word as well as a glyph — or a legend/coach that names all five — fitting a 40mm screen without truncation
- [ ] Air mouse and Drag lock state their ON state in words, not tint alone: colour washes out outdoors and roughly one man in twelve cannot separate the orange from the blue
- [ ] Control answers "what can I do here?" without entering a mode: a help affordance lists the five controls, the crown's job, the long press into Read, and tap-tap to right-click
- [ ] Screenshots from both a 40mm and a 49mm simulator in the PR showing no truncation at the largest supported Dynamic Type size

## Where it stands today — `partial`
Watch/RemoteView.swift:933-965 — the five controls are still glyph-only (`primaryClickButton`, `padButton("gyroscope", …)`, `padButton(remote.dragLocked ? "lock.fill" : "lock.open", …)`, `padButton("keyboard", "Type")`, an ellipsis.circle NavigationLink); the words are passed only to `.accessibilityLabel` (Watch/RemoteView.swift:978, 1005-1012), which VoiceOver speaks but nothing draws. DONE half: Watch/RemoteView.swift:866-869 states both ON states in words on the trackpad — `Text("drag held — tap the lock to release")` and `Text("air mouse — point your arm")`. Tap-tap right-click is named at Watch/RemoteView.swift:876 (`Text("tap · tap-tap right-clicks")`). No help affordance exists on the Control screen: the only helpSheet is on SessionsView (Watch/WatchViews.swift:765-785) and it names Control Mac/Inspect, not the five controls (grep for `help|legend|coach` in Watch/RemoteView.swift returns only comments).

**What is actually left:** Visible words (or a legend) for all five controls, a "?" help affordance on the Control screen itself listing the five plus the crown's job and the long press into Read, and the 40mm/49mm largest-Dynamic-Type screenshots.

title: Snap the terminal back to the newest line after you send anything
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `A7`.

## The problem
"When I press continue, I'm just moving in. I'm again forced to scroll all the way down." Scrolling up to read correctly stops the auto-follow (FollowsTail), but sending Continue, Enter or a reply is the clearest possible statement of "show me what happens next" — and nothing re-arms it. So every command is followed by hand-scrolling to the bottom.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Every send path in AgentLiveView (Continue, Enter, Reply, the terminal key-bar chips, Insert clipboard) re-arms followTail and scrolls the output to the "tail" anchor within one poll
- [ ] Scrolling up still stops the auto-follow, so reading back an error that scrolled past is not taken away
- [ ] Opening the full terminal from the Output section always lands on the newest line, not wherever the last visit left it
- [ ] Proof on a real session that prints continuously: scroll up 20 lines, tap Enter, and the newest line is on screen without touching the crown

## Where it stands today — `missing`
Watch/WatchViews.swift:885 declares `@State private var followTail = true`; grep across Watch/WatchViews.swift shows it is written in exactly two places, both `.onAppear` (Watch/WatchViews.swift:1179 and 1214). No send path touches it: Continue/Enter/Reply/Insert-clipboard at Watch/WatchViews.swift:992-1016 call `store.send(...)` only, `sendReply` at Watch/WatchViews.swift:1155-1160 only clears the draft, and all sixteen terminal key-bar chips at Watch/WatchViews.swift:1246-1261 call `store.send(key:)` with no re-arm. The follow guard at Watch/WatchViews.swift:1184 and 1216 (`guard followTail else { return }`) therefore stays false after a scroll-up until the sheet is reopened.

**What is actually left:** Re-arm followTail (and scroll to the "tail" anchor) from every send path. The one criterion already satisfied is the last-listed one: opening the terminal sheet lands at the newest line, via `.onAppear { followTail = true; proxy.scrollTo("tail", …) }` at Watch/WatchViews.swift:1179/1214.

title: Use the watch's own gestures, with visible state for each
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `A13`.

## The problem
"Make sure we are maximizing the options we have when it comes to watch — pressing the button, hold press, and double tap." Today exactly one control claims Double Tap (handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction) on the Click button in RemoteView) and exactly one long press exists (the screen preview into Read mode). On the screens that matter most — the "Needs you" row, the live session — the wrist gesture does nothing, and nothing on screen ever tells you a gesture is available.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Each primary screen names one Double Tap action and claims it with handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction): Approve on AttentionRow, Continue in AgentLiveView, Click on Control
- [ ] Every screen with an armed Double Tap shows an indicator saying what it will do, so the gesture is discoverable without documentation
- [ ] Long press has a documented meaning wherever it is added and keeps its Read-mode meaning on the preview; it never collides with the trackpad's minimumDistance-0 drag
- [ ] No gesture is the only way to reach an action — each one also has a visible button. Hand-checked on a Series 9 or later, because the simulator cannot fire Double Tap

## Where it stands today — `partial`
DONE: Watch/RemoteView.swift:970-985 — `primaryClickButton` claims the gesture with `button.handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction)` under `if #available(watchOS 11.0, *)`, and it has a visible button. The Read-mode long press is kept at Watch/RemoteView.swift:805 (`.onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.4) { enterInspect() }`). NOT DONE: repo-wide grep across Watch/ shows `handGestureShortcut` appears exactly once (Watch/RemoteView.swift:981) and `onLongPressGesture` exactly once (Watch/RemoteView.swift:805). AttentionRow (Watch/WatchViews.swift:362) claims no gesture; AgentLiveView's Continue (Watch/WatchViews.swift:992-996) claims none. Nothing on any screen renders a Double Tap indicator — the only on-screen gesture text is the trackpad's "tap · tap-tap right-clicks" (Watch/RemoteView.swift:876), which is about touch, not the wrist gesture.

**What is actually left:** Claim .primaryAction on AttentionRow's Approve and AgentLiveView's Continue, add the visible "what Double Tap will do" indicator on each armed screen, and the Series 9+ hand-check.

title: Wake a sleeping machine from the wrist
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **A** (control surface & input), items `buried-wake-on-lan`.

## The problem
The iPhone has a working "Wake via <peer>" button (WakeRow); the watch has no wake affordance at all, even though WatchMeshStore already carries the MAC address for exactly this path and the daemon already serves POST /wake. So a machine that went to sleep is a machine the wrist cannot bring back — which is precisely the moment the phone is in another room.

## The problem

title: Read x-mesh-rect on iOS instead of guessing the crop from aspect
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.
> Source: round **E** (capture hierarchy), items `E1, E2`.

## The problem
On the phone, zooming into the Mac sometimes sharpens and sometimes silently does nothing, with no message either way. iOS/RemoteScreenView.swift asks for a region with screenImage (bytes only) and then infers whether the daemon actually cropped by comparing the picture's aspect to the display's (servedLooksLikeCrop / cropIsDistinguishable). Any region whose shape is close to the display's is declared indistinguishable and the crop is not even requested (line 217) — so on an iPad, or a phone whose screen surface matches the Mac's proportions, region capture is off and text never gets clearer. MeshClient.screenFrame already returns the daemon's own answer.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Zooming past 1.05x against a 0.5.0 daemon requests a region at every container/display aspect combination, including a container aspect exactly equal to the display's — the case that is silently skipped today.
- [ ] A check runs the shipped decision and fails if a frame with no x-mesh-rect header is ever drawn as a crop, or if a frame with one is ever zoomed a second time.
- [ ] A daemon that declines the crop still draws the full frame with client-side zoom, and a tap still places the pointer under the finger at any zoom.

title: Send the daemon's served rect through the phone relay
body:

## The problem
When the watch is off the Tailnet it gets the Mac's screen through the iPhone. The phone already asks the Mac for the exact rectangle the watch is looking at, but it hands the watch bare JPEG bytes and throws away the x-mesh-rect header that says which rectangle came back. The watch therefore cannot tell a crop from a whole screen, so today it deliberately stops asking for one on the relay route (Watch/RemoteView.swift:469-476) and goes back to magnifying a 600px downsample. Off-tailnet, zooming into the Mac still shows mush — the exact complaint region capture was built to fix.

- [ ] MeshSnapshot carries the served rect (nil = whole display), populated in iOS/MeshStore.swift from MeshClient.screenFrame's x-mesh-rect header instead of screenImage's bare bytes.
- [ ] In Inspect over the relay the watch sends its visibleRegion and draws the reply through frameTransform(servedRect:zoom:pan:), so a served crop renders at 1x with zero pan — the rule the direct path already passes in scripts/check-inspect-crop.sh, extended to cover the relay path.
- [ ] A relayed frame stays under the 262,144-byte WCSession message cap at every zoom level; a check computes the worst case (a 6x crop of a 6K display at the relay's width/quality clamp) and fails if it would exceed the cap.
- [ ] Against a daemon without the screenRegion capability the relay sends no rect and the watch behaves exactly as it does today: full frame, client-side zoom, and never a crop it only inferred.

title: Stream frames over one connection instead of re-polling
body:
> Auto-drafted from a spoken backlog on 2026-08-27, then graded against the code.

## The problem
The phone asks for a brand new frame every 350ms (iOS/RemoteScreenView.swift:145-149). - [ ] Capture stops within one frame of the client disconnecting; a check opens the stream, aborts it, and asserts no screencapture process and no capture loop survives.
- [ ] Frame pacing is decided server-side and bounded, and consecutive identical frames are skipped rather than re-sent.
- [ ] `screenStream` is advertised in CAPABILITIES and the existing /screen.jpg polling route is left untouched so old clients are unaffected.
